arguments.conclusion: The Federal Reserve's ending of quantitative tightening and implementation of operation twist (selling MBS, buying T-bills) will ease liquidity conditions broadly, despite continued tightening in MBS.

arguments.premise_synthesis: The Fed ended quantitative tightening at its last meeting and will, starting December 1st, continue selling mortgage-backed securities while using the proceeds to purchase Treasury bills. This operation drains liquidity from the MBS market but injects it into the T-bill market, which is more directly tied to fiscal policy and overall financial conditions, thereby easing liquidity conditions broadly.
arguments.conclusion_supported: This specific policy action is an application of the canonical central claim, demonstrating that deficit spending forces the Fed to adopt unconventional balance sheet policies that inject liquidity into the financial system, which risks inflation, erosion of dollar purchasing power, and a wealth transfer from savers to borrowers.
